raw_case_text: A 37-year-old foreign domestic worker with no history of major infection and 3 previous vaginal births presented with a one-week history of suprapubic pain associated with fever. The patient also experienced loss of appetite and loss of weight. On examination, she was tachycardic with high-grade fever of 38.9 C. Abdomen examination revealed tenderness over her suprapubic area; however, pelvic examination showed no abnormality. Her total white cell count was 5.9 x 109/L, with predominantly lymphocytes (16.5 x 109/L) and monocytes (2.6 x 109/L). Her C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) were elevated at 29.9 mg/dl and 100 mm/Hr. Chest radiograph showed bilateral perihilar opacities which could represent enlarged hilar nodes. There was no evidence of fibrosis, pleural effusion, or infective changes (Figure 1). Ultrasound scan showed presence of right complex mass measured 12 x 6 x 6 cm with minimal free fluid at the pouch of Douglas. Cancer antigen 125 (CA 125) was elevated at 97 u/ml. Working diagnosis of tuboovarian abscess was made, and she was treated with a broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotic. Despite 48 hours of parenteral antibiotic, she did not improve clinically. After discussion, she opted for exploratory laparotomy. There were moderate amount of ascitic fluid with the presence of slough and cheesy materials covering the entire abdominal and pelvic cavities. However, there was no tubercle noted over the peritoneal surface. There was a right ovarian cyst measuring 12 x 6 cm and features suggestive of a mature cystic teratoma. Right salpingo-oophorectomy was performed (Figure 2). Peritoneal fluid cytology showed no malignant cells, and there was no acid-fast bacilli (AFB) seen on AFB staining. Mycobacterium culture did not yield any positive AFB even after 6 weeks. In view of high index of suspicion for TB, peritoneal fluid was also sent for polymerase chain reaction (semiauto TB PCR machine, Rotor-Gene Q , Qiagen) testing, which was positive for NTM but negative for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Bronchoalveolar lavage was done as the patient was unable to produce sputum, which was negative for TB as well. Infective screening such as HIV, venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL), and hepatitis was nonreactive. Histopathological examination confirmed a right mature cystic teratoma. She remained well postoperatively and completed intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole for 10 days. She was initially planned for anti-TB (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and streptomycin) following positive PCR testing for NTB. However, upon discharge, she was sent back to home town immediately by her employer. Hence, we have no further information about her progress.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 37-year-old female presented with a 1-week history of suprapubic pain, high-grade fever, loss of appetite, and weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 37-year-old female domestic worker presented with a 1-week history of worsening suprapubic abdominal pain accompanied by high-grade fever, anorexia, and weight loss. She had no relief after 48 hours of broad-spectrum parenteral antibiotics for presumed tubo-ovarian abscess, prompting surgical exploration.
subjective.past_medical_history: Foreign domestic worker; para 3 (3 previous spontaneous vaginal deliveries). No history of major infections or tuberculosis contacts.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for suprapubic pain, high-grade fever, anorexia, and weight loss. Negative for abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Tachycardic, febrile with temperature of 38.9 °C. Abdomen: marked tenderness over suprapubic region. Pelvic examination normal.
objective.routine_investigations: White blood cell count 5.9 x 109/L (predominantly lymphocytes 16.5 x 109/L, monocytes 2.6 x 109/L), CRP 29.9 mg/dL, ESR 100 mm/h. Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125) elevated at 97 U/mL. Serologic screening for HIV, syphilis (VDRL), and viral hepatitis non-reactive. Chest radiograph: bilateral perihilar opacities suggestive of hilar adenopathy, without pulmonary infiltrates, cavities, or pleural effusion. Pelvic ultrasound: 12 x 6 x 6 cm right complex adnexal mass with minimal free fluid in pouch of Douglas.
objective.advanced_workup: Exploratory laparotomy with right salpingo-oophorectomy: cheesy exudate coating abdominal and pelvic cavities without discrete peritoneal tubercles; 12 x 6 cm right ovarian mass. Histopathology confirmed benign mature cystic teratoma. Peritoneal fluid cytology negative for malignant cells; acid-fast staining showed no acid-fast bacilli; 6-week mycobacterial cultures were negative. Bronchoalveolar lavage was negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Mature cystic teratoma of the right ovary with coexisting pelvic/peritoneal mycobacterial infection, confirmed by ovarian histopathology demonstrating benign mature cystic teratoma and peritoneal fluid PCR (Rotor-Gene Q) testing positive for non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) while negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Acid-fast stains and 6-week mycobacterial cultures were negative. Initial presentation mimicked tubo-ovarian abscess and peritoneal tuberculosis. Management & Outcome: Treated surgically with right salpingo-oophorectomy and completed a 10-day course of intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole. Antituberculous therapy (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, streptomycin) was planned based on positive mycobacterial PCR, but the patient was repatriated to her home country upon discharge.
